scope: One command connects prepared source exchange, bounded negotiation, fulfillment, checks, and synthetic payment.
new_trade_cases: Replace a rejected source, accept a counterproposal, pay, and grant both downloads through one command.
Reject negotiation without constructing the payment worker.
Reject an excessive amount before model or payment requests.
Complete one permitted rework without another command.
Void authorization after the second rejected output without capture or a third attempt.
Recover a lost capture response through the same transaction without another payment mutation.
Stop after model failure without payment or secret disclosure.
Warn that payment can complete after interruption.

tdd.before_implementation: The primary trade test failed because argparse rejected the missing trade command.
tdd.after_implementation: All 21 Gemini runtime tests and all 559 repository tests passed.

limits: The operator prepares complete permitted candidates, account bindings, source files, and valid Mandates before starting the command.
Scripted decisions replace Gemini and local responses replace PayPal in this check.
A zero process exit code does not establish payment completion. Inspect execution.status.
Partially completed negotiation requires inspection. Recover uncertain payments through work with the same finalized transaction.
The amount option limits each candidate. It does not reset cumulative authorization.
This check does not measure customer savings or implement arbitrary natural-language condition conversion.
This change does not grant independent review acceptance, G4 acceptance, G5 acceptance, or production eligibility.

language_review.scope: Changed runtime messages, command instructions, status prose, design connections, and evidence descriptions.
language_review.checks: Manual terminology and meaning review plus sentence, local-link, and whitespace checks.
exceptions: The user requested Korean prose in user-checklist.ko.md. Exact commands, paths, and identifiers retain their required forms.
